title: Fiber Cement Board vs Gypsum Board: Which is Right for Your Project?
description: A technical comparison of fiber cement and gypsum board for European construction — fire performance, moisture resistance, weight, and CE compliance.
author: Terasun Europe Technical Team
body:
## Introduction

Fiber cement board and gypsum board are both widely used in European construction, but they serve different purposes and perform very differently in demanding conditions.

## Key Differences

**Moisture resistance**: Fiber cement board (Terasun TSM) is dimensionally stable in wet and humid conditions. Gypsum board swells, degrades, and can fail when exposed to sustained moisture. For wet rooms, bathrooms, and exterior applications, fiber cement is the correct choice.

**Fire performance**: Terasun TSM achieves E 120 / EI 90 / EW 120 fire resistance in tested wall systems. This is system-level performance, independently verified by test report FIRES-CR-284-25-AUPE.

**Weight**: Terasun TSM at 12 mm weighs 9.96 kg/m², which is heavier than standard gypsum board but provides greater rigidity and impact resistance.

**CE compliance**: Both products can carry CE marking. Terasun TSM is CE marked under 1023-CPR-1565 P with ETA 24/0895.

## When to Specify Fiber Cement

- Exterior facade cladding
- Wet rooms and bathrooms
- Fire-rated partition walls
- Industrial and commercial applications requiring impact resistance
- Projects requiring EPD documentation for LEED/BREEAM
